what_it_does: UV filter that helps protect skin from UVB and short UVA rays.
summary_short: Octocrylene is a sunscreen filter used to boost SPF and help stabilize avobenzone for broader UV protection. It is generally considered safe up to 10% in cosmetics, though rare photoallergic reactions can occur, especially in people sensitized to ketoprofen.
summary_long:
Octocrylene is an organic sunscreen filter that mainly absorbs UVB and short UVA wavelengths. In formulas, it helps raise sun protection and is often used because it can stabilize avobenzone, a UVA filter that otherwise breaks down more easily in sunlight [PMID:unknown].

For everyday use, the main benefit is photoprotection: sunscreens help reduce sunburn and support protection against UV-related skin aging and some forms of skin cancer when applied generously and reapplied regularly [PMID:unknown]. Octocrylene is usually part of a filter blend rather than the only active sunscreen ingredient.

The safety data summarized in a 2019 review found no endocrine-disruption potential and considered octocrylene safe as a cosmetic UV filter up to 10% [PMID:unknown]. Allergic reactions appear uncommon, but photoallergy has been reported more often than regular contact allergy, particularly in people with prior photosensitization to ketoprofen [PMID:unknown].

Octocrylene is commonly paired with avobenzone because it improves formula stability and helps support broader UVA/UVB coverage. It may be less ideal for users with a known sunscreen photoallergy history or ketoprofen-related photosensitivity.

Environmental research has detected octocrylene in water sources and fish, and recent reviews note concern about possible marine ecosystem effects [PMID:unknown]. For users prioritizing reef or marine-impact concerns, octocrylene-free sunscreens may be preferred, while still maintaining consistent sun protection.
